The startup creates 1 mm gut organoids for drug and compound testing, selling its GastroScreen platform.
The competition featured 20 startups, narrowed to five finalists, and judged by VCs and TechCrunch editors.
Battlefield alumni have raised over $30 billion and secured more than 200 exits.

posts.title: Bluesky expands its AI-powered Attie app to let anyone build websites, games, and more | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Bluesky has expanded its experimental Attie platform to let anyone build interactive experiences such as websites, games, quizzes, and polls, moving beyond its original AI‑powered custom social feeds. The new tool runs on the AT Protocol, giving creators built‑in distribution across Bluesky’s decentralized social network and tying projects to users’ ATProto identities. Creators can bring their own AI models or use open‑weight options, and Attie will suggest projects based on public Bluesky profiles. CEO Toni Schneider, who has taken over as interim chief after Jay Graber’s departure, says the move is part of Bluesky’s push to revitalize engagement and support developers in the AI era.
key_points: Attie now supports building websites, games, quizzes, and polls for everyday users
Projects built with Attie run on AT Protocol, giving them built‑in distribution across Bluesky’s network
Creators can use their own AI models or open‑weight options and receive suggestions based on their Bluesky profiles
Toni Schneider, Bluesky’s interim CEO, is steering the company toward an AI‑focused future

posts.title: Meet the five companies competing in the Startup Battlefield finals at Disrupt 2026 | TechCrunch
posts.author: Anthony Ha
posts.summary: TechCrunch’s Disrupt 2026 will feature five finalists in the Startup Battlefield finals, representing four categories: space and physical AI, energy and manufacturing, health tech and life sciences, and enterprise and security. The finalists include Apate, which deploys AI agents to bait scammers; Flox Intelligence, which uses edge AI to deter wildlife; Intero Biosystems, which creates multi‑cell intestinal organoids for drug testing; Industrial Next, which offers AI‑driven robotic stations that can be retooled in minutes; and Satlyt, which builds software for shared satellite computing. The finals begin tomorrow at 11:30 a.m. Pacific, with a panel of judges selecting a winner who receives the Startup Battlefield Cup and $100,000 equity‑free. This lineup showcases a broad spectrum of emerging technologies, from AI‑powered fraud prevention to advanced biomedical models and autonomous manufacturing solutions.

Apate uses AI agents to bait and study scammers
Intero Biosystems develops multi‑cell intestinal organoids for more accurate drug testing
Industrial Next offers AI‑driven robotic stations that can be retooled in minutes

posts.title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film 'the right way' and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: Mark Wahlberg spoke at TechCrunch Disrupt about his view that AI can be a useful tool in filmmaking when used responsibly, such as enhancing set design for his upcoming Pete Rose biopic. He stressed that AI should not replace real actors or generate full scripts, but rather augment the creative process while keeping storytelling at the core. Wahlberg also expressed openness to creating an AI likeness of himself for future projects, including his animated series "Ted," to preserve his legacy. He has not yet used the CAA Vault but would consider it if it allows his descendants to manage his image responsibly.
key_points: Wahlberg supports AI for enhancing film elements, not for replacing actors or writing scripts
He is open to using an AI likeness of himself for future projects and legacy preservation
He prioritizes storytelling over effects-driven filmmaking
He has not used the CAA Vault yet but would consider it for managing his image

posts.title: Bluesky wants to make it easier to buy, sell, and fundraise on the network | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: Bluesky announced it will roll out payments in the coming months to enable buying, selling, and fundraising directly on its decentralized network, a move that bypasses traditional advertising revenue. The company’s CEO Toni Schneider explained that the new monetization model will be transparent and designed to benefit creators, aligning with Bluesky’s public‑benefit corporation status. By building on existing commerce activity, Bluesky aims to disrupt the infrastructure layer of social media rather than just adding another app. The announcement marks a significant shift toward infrastructure‑level revenue models for decentralized platforms.
key_points: Bluesky will introduce payments to enable buying, selling, and fundraising on its decentralized network.
Monetization will be designed to benefit creators and avoid traditional advertising.
CEO Toni Schneider, former Automattic CEO, leads the initiative after taking over in March.
The company’s public‑benefit corporation structure guides its revenue strategy.

posts.title: Anthropic is letting METR researchers look under the hood with employee-level access | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aditya Mehta
posts.summary: Anthropic has announced that six researchers from the nonprofit METR will receive employee‑level access to its internal tools, office space, and laptops to independently evaluate the company’s frontier AI models, safety protocols, and risk management. The move comes amid a wave of incidents where AI agents acted outside their instructions, prompting calls for greater transparency and external oversight. Anthropic likens the arrangement to banking regulators placing resident examiners inside major banks, and it has agreed to allow METR to publish its findings without veto power, except for narrowly defined redactions. This initiative fulfills a promise made by CEO Dario Amodei in a September essay and aligns with a White House accord that encourages AI firms to embed outside evaluators in their labs.
key_points: Anthropic grants METR researchers employee‑level access to assess its AI models and safety practices
METR is free to publish its assessments without Anthropic’s veto, only limited redactions are allowed
The arrangement mirrors banking regulator practices and is part of Anthropic’s tiered evaluator system
The move follows CEO Amodei’s September essay and a White House accord on independent AI review

posts.title: Governments are hacking people with 'zero-click' spyware by showing them online ads | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: Security researchers at Citizen Lab have revealed that an Israeli advertising company, Discover‑Tech, is being used by government‑backed spyware makers to deliver zero‑click malware through online ads. The study shows that spyware firms Candiru and Bindecy exploited Discover‑Tech’s Controlium platform to target specific devices worldwide, infecting at least 45 Windows computers at Al Jazeera in 2024‑2025. The attacks demonstrate that malicious code can be embedded in ads that reach military, government, and critical‑infrastructure devices, raising the risk of widespread covert surveillance. Citizen Lab urges users to disable ad tracking or block ads entirely to protect themselves from this emerging threat.
key_points: Discover‑Tech’s ad platform is being used to deliver zero‑click spyware to targeted devices worldwide.
Citizen Lab’s report documents at least 45 Al Jazeera Windows computers infected via Candiru spyware in 2024‑2025.
The malicious ads were shown on devices used by militaries, governments, and critical infrastructure, indicating a broad potential impact.
The findings highlight the need for stronger ad‑blocking and tracking‑disabling measures to defend against covert government‑backed hacking.

posts.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lucas Ropek
posts.summary: Meta has unveiled Muse Spark Open, an 816‑billion‑parameter open‑weight AI model built to run natively on Apple hardware. The multimodal system supports coding, agentic workflows, and even video‑editing tasks, but it demands at least 1 TB of RAM and performs best on a Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra chip. By offering an open‑weight alternative, Meta aims to give developers cost‑effective, transparent, and flexible AI tools that can be deployed locally. The model is now available through several API platforms for developers and enterprises.
key_points: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816‑billion‑parameter open‑weight AI model for Macs

Open‑weight models provide cost efficiency, transparency, and flexibility for developers

posts.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Panos Panay, unveiled the company’s new Bee ambient AI wearables at TechCrunch Disrupt, positioning them as the next step in personal computing that moves away from app‑centric interactions toward devices that anticipate user needs. The Bee band and credit‑card‑sized sensor attach quietly to the body or phone, passively record audio, process it in real time, delete raw data, and store only encrypted transcripts that the user controls. Panay emphasized privacy as a core design principle and outlined a vision where a network of sensor‑driven devices, linked by an intelligence layer, will gradually reduce the need to explicitly launch apps. While Amazon still sees smartphones as important, the company is betting on a future of ambient, AI‑powered devices that keep users present and productive.
key_points: Amazon launches Bee ambient AI wearables that record audio in real time, delete raw data, and encrypt transcripts controlled by the user.
Panos Panay envisions a shift to ambient computing where devices anticipate user needs instead of relying on app commands.
Privacy is built into Bee devices, with no raw audio storage and user‑controlled encryption.
Amazon sees future devices as sensor‑driven, linked by an intelligence layer that connects multiple form factors.

posts.title: Ramp reaches $60B valuation as it pushes deeper into AI | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ram Iyer
posts.summary: Ramp raised $1.85 billion in a new funding round that values the expense‑management startup at $60 billion, up from $44 billion just four months earlier. The company reports annualized revenue exceeding $2 billion, a 25% faster growth rate than a year ago, and 85,000 customers including Visa, Uber, and Shopify. Ramp is broadening its product suite beyond expense management into payments, fraud detection, procurement, and AI‑driven tools, launching a corporate credit card for AI agents and a model‑routing service for AI inference. The expansion positions Ramp in direct competition with Rippling and, according to investor Keith Rabois, may bring it into conflict with AI firm Anthropic over token‑spend management.
key_points: $1.85B round values Ramp at $60B
Annualized revenue >$2B with 25% faster growth and 85k customers
Ramp is expanding into payments, procurement, and AI‑centric products
Competition with Rippling and potential clash with Anthropic over AI token spend

posts.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay on the importance of failure and bouncing back from it | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: Amazon SVP of Devices, Alexa, and Leo Panos Panay told startup founders at TechCrunch Disrupt that failure is an inevitable and essential part of building a successful product. He drew on his own experience at Microsoft, where the launch of the Surface RT tablet led to a nearly $1 billion write‑down and a public label of failure. Panay urged founders to admit mistakes, harvest the lessons learned, and adjust their vision by small, deliberate shifts rather than abandoning it entirely. By embracing failure and learning quickly, he believes companies can accelerate progress and stay resilient in the face of setbacks.
key_points: Panay stresses that failure is necessary for innovation and product success.
He cites the Surface RT failure at Microsoft, which cost nearly $1 billion, as a key lesson.
Founders should harvest lessons, avoid excuses, and adjust their vision by small, deliberate changes.
Embracing failure accelerates progress and builds resilience in startups.

posts.title: SK Hynix bargains for chip equipment exports to its China facility in return for building a factory in US | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kate Park
posts.summary: SK Hynix’s flash‑memory unit Solidigm is seeking U.S. approval to ship advanced chip‑making equipment to its Dalian, China, plant as a condition for building a new NAND flash factory in the United States, likely in upstate New York. The move comes amid a global NAND shortage that has pushed prices up 15% to 20% in the fourth quarter, and reflects Washington’s push to bring more semiconductor manufacturing to America. Solidigm plans a 2027 U.S. IPO that could raise about $10 billion and value the company at up to $100 billion. The request follows tightened U.S. export rules on advanced chips and the revocation of special exemptions for Chinese facilities in 2025, though annual licenses have been granted to SK Hynix and Samsung for equipment shipments to China.
key_points: Solidigm wants to ship U.S. chip‑making equipment to its Dalian plant to boost NAND production, pending U.S. approval.
The U.S. government is encouraging SK Hynix to build a new NAND factory in the U.S., possibly in upstate New York, as part of a broader chip‑manufacturing strategy.
Solidigm is preparing for a 2027 U.S. IPO that could raise around $10 billion and value the company at up to $100 billion.
U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips were tightened in 2023 and special exemptions were revoked in 2025, but annual licenses remain in place for SK Hynix and Samsung.

posts.title: Google’s Universal Cart shopping tool launches in the US | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lauren Forristal
posts.summary: Google has rolled out its Universal Cart tool to U.S. users, allowing shoppers to save items from multiple retailers across search and the Gemini app and revisit them later without losing progress. The cart tracks price drops and stock availability, and can suggest payment methods that leverage credit‑card perks and surface promo codes. It is built on Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol, an open standard aimed at unifying AI agents and retailers throughout the shopping journey. The launch underscores Google’s push to embed AI into e‑commerce, joining features like conversational product discovery and AI‑powered store‑inquiry tools.
key_points: Universal Cart lets users save and manage items from multiple retailers across search and Gemini.
The tool notifies users of price drops, restocks, and offers tailored payment and promo‑code suggestions.
It operates under Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol, an open standard for AI‑driven shopping.
The launch is part of Google’s broader AI‑powered e‑commerce strategy.

posts.title: Volvo makes a bigger bet on Nvidia for hands-free automated driving | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: Volvo has deepened its decade‑long partnership with Nvidia, committing to use Nvidia’s Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, Alpamayo software stack, and Halos safety layer in future vehicles. The collaboration will enable an automated driving system capable of navigating both urban streets and highways, with Volvo integrating its safety systems and engineering expertise. While the exact value and first vehicle model remain undisclosed, Volvo plans to debut the new tech stack in a brand‑new vehicle within the next decade, expanding the approach to all powertrains, not just electric. The move signals Volvo’s shift toward a full‑tech‑stack strategy and a broader rollout of Nvidia’s autonomous‑driving platform across its lineup.
key_points: Volvo expands its partnership with Nvidia to include Hyperion, Alpamayo, and Halos for future automated driving.
The new stack will support navigation on urban streets and highways across all vehicle types, not just EVs.
Volvo plans to debut the technology in a new vehicle within the next decade, though the first model is not yet announced.
The collaboration reflects Volvo’s shift to a full‑tech‑stack approach and broader use of Nvidia’s autonomous platform.

posts.title: AI agents are coming to Rivian's cars | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: Rivian has launched an AI assistant that lets drivers and passengers control the vehicle with voice commands and plans to allow third‑party agents such as Anthropic’s Claude, OpenAI’s Dots, and Meta’s Muse in the future. The company built its own agentic framework that decides whether to run a local model or send a request to the cloud, routing actions like temperature control or news summaries to the appropriate software component. Safety concerns keep vehicle‑level controls out of the agents’ reach, so the system will act as an extension of existing apps rather than a direct driver of the car. Rivian aims to weave context from other devices into the assistant, enabling richer, cross‑platform interactions while coordinating with external labs for plumbing and compliance.
key_points: Rivian’s AI assistant can handle voice commands and will soon support third‑party agents like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta
The company built an in‑house agentic framework that routes requests to local or cloud models
Safety constraints prevent agents from controlling vehicle‑level functions such as braking or steering
Rivian plans to integrate context from other devices for richer, cross‑platform interactions

posts.title: Ricursive Intelligence is betting on AI-designed chips to help solve the compute crisis | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: Ricursive Intelligence, founded by Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini, is developing AI that designs chips, learning from each iteration to accelerate and automate the process. At TechCrunch Disrupt, the founders highlighted that AI-designed chips could meet the projected 10,000‑fold increase in compute demand over five years without expanding data center footprints. By optimizing entire chips rather than partitioning them, the AI can discover unconventional layouts—such as a donut‑shaped AlphaChip—that outperform traditional designs. The company argues that rapid, efficient chip design will enable custom, energy‑efficient hardware for emerging applications like AR, VR, and biological computing.
key_points: AI-driven chip design can reduce design time from years to weeks, enabling rapid prototyping for niche applications.
Ricursive’s approach optimizes whole chips, producing unconventional layouts that outperform traditional block‑based designs.
The startup believes AI-designed chips will help meet a projected 10,000‑fold compute demand increase without expanding data center infrastructure.

posts.title: Figma announces new features to define how agents work on its platform | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Figma unveiled a suite of new tools at its first Config event in India, including a Markdown‑based editor called Figma Specs that lets teams codify their design language and guide AI agents. The company also opened its code layers feature to public beta, enabling designers to embed code directly on the canvas and ask agents to generate or modify code for prototypes. Integration with the headless CMS Payload and support for over 20 new MCP partners expands Figma’s content and AI ecosystem, while the India launch underscores the platform’s growing presence in the country’s largest market outside the U.S. These updates aim to make AI‑driven design more predictable and aligned with brand rules.

Code layers beta lets designers embed code on canvas and convert designs to code via agents
Integration with Payload CMS and MCP partners broadens content and AI tool capabilities
India event highlighted wider agent availability and Figma’s strong foothold in India’s top 100 companies

posts.title: Gudea leverages AI to help organizations prevent social media crises before they erupt | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lauren Forristal
posts.summary: Gudea, a 2023‑founded startup, uses AI to map how rumors and misinformation spread across more than 500 online platforms, giving brands context beyond simple mention counts so they can preempt crises. The company, which has nearly 40 clients including Fortune 50 firms and government agencies, raised $7 million in seed funding led by Mudita Venture Partners and Silicon Road Ventures, bringing its total capital to about $15 million. Gudea’s technology analyzes relationships, pathways, and inauthentic activity, and plans next‑year geolocation features that pinpoint conversations to city‑block level. The tool is positioned to help organizations respond proactively as generative‑AI‑driven content makes online manipulation easier and more widespread.
key_points: Gudea maps rumor spread across 500+ sites, offering context beyond raw metrics to help brands preempt crises.
The startup has 40 clients, including Fortune 50 firms, and raised $7M seed, totaling $15M in funding.
Its AI analyzes relationships and inauthentic activity, and will add city‑block‑level geolocation next year.

posts.title: Hiyd is a health tracker that attaches to the watch you already wear | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: Hiyd has unveiled a slim, 0.3‑mm disc that attaches to the back of a watch using microsuction, allowing users to track heart rate, sleep, movement, calories and VO₂ max without sacrificing style. The sensor, 2.7 mm thick and 7 g, syncs data to an iOS or Android app and is trained with AI on labeled activity footage. Founder Salah Batroukh, a former Apple design engineer, emphasizes invisible health tracking and plans to add nutrition insights that tie eating habits to sleep and performance. Hiyd will showcase its device at TechCrunch Disrupt, is a top‑20 Startup Battlefield competitor, and aims to launch a Kickstarter in November after securing over 16,000 deposits.
key_points: Hiyd’s microsuction disc lets users wear a health sensor on any watch without magnets or adhesive.
The 7‑gram sensor captures standard wearable metrics and uses AI‑trained data sets for accurate activity classification.
Founder Salah Batroukh, ex‑Apple engineer, focuses on unobtrusive design and plans to add nutrition‑linked sleep insights.
The startup is competing in Startup Battlefield and plans a Kickstarter launch in November with 16,000 pre‑orders.

posts.title: Amazon's Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75 | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Amazon’s personal AI wearable brand Bee has unveiled two new devices, the Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse, marking its first product releases since the company’s acquisition by Amazon last year. The Frontier, priced at $74.99, is a wrist‑worn or clip‑on device that offers IP67 water resistance, seven days of battery life, and advanced noise‑filtered microphones, while the Eclipse is a credit‑card‑sized phone attachment costing $99.99. Both devices capture conversations in real time, generate free summaries, and, with an $11.99 monthly Bee Pro subscription, provide unlimited summaries, to‑do suggestions, and integrations with Amazon.com, Alexa+, and third‑party productivity apps. Bee emphasizes privacy by processing audio locally, encrypting transcripts with device‑generated keys, and allowing users to delete data at any time, while optional Alexa Voice ID can enable hands‑free interaction and Amazon purchases.
key_points: Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse launch at $74.99 and $99.99, respectively, expanding Bee’s lineup after Amazon’s acquisition
Both devices offer free conversation summaries and a $11.99/month Bee Pro plan that unlocks unlimited summaries, to‑do lists, and Amazon/Alexa integrations
Privacy is built in: audio is processed locally, transcripts are encrypted with device‑controlled keys, and users can delete data anytime
The devices integrate with Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, and Apple HealthKit, and the Frontier includes IP67 water resistance and a seven‑day battery life

posts.title: Flock CEO says its microphones detect 'just gunshots' — its website says different | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: Flock’s CEO Garrett Langley told TechCrunch Disrupt that the company’s microphones only detect gunshots, a claim that contrasts with the company’s website, which advertises detection of gunfire, car crashes, fireworks and other ambient sounds. The company’s Gunshot Detection feature, launched last year, was criticized for listening to human voices; after backlash it removed the distress‑detection capability and clarified that it does not monitor conversations. Protesters in San Francisco gathered outside the venue as privacy groups and the ACLU called for tighter oversight, and several states have already ended contracts with Flock. Despite the controversy, Langley maintains that the system’s primary purpose is public‑safety alerts and that its microphone network is comparable to ShotSpotter’s 25,000‑unit array.
key_points: Flock’s CEO insists the microphones only detect gunshots, while the website claims broader ambient‑sound detection.
The company removed its human‑distress detection feature after privacy groups condemned it for listening to voices.
Protests and state cancellations highlight growing public and regulatory scrutiny of Flock’s surveillance technology.
Flock’s microphone count is similar to ShotSpotter’s 25,000‑unit network as of 2024.

posts.title: Colossal Biosciences announces new AI platform to help accelerate de-extinction efforts | TechCrunch
posts.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
posts.summary: Colossal Biosciences unveiled GenoMorph, an AI platform that uses 3D morphology, comparative genomics, and developmental biology to pinpoint gene edits for extinct species with sparse genomic data, notably the dodo. The system, built on data from over 70 bird species and developmental studies of chickens, quail, ducks, and pigeons, has identified roughly 2,300 promising DNA targets for dodo cranial morphology and will test them using a lipid‑nanoparticle delivery method. In parallel, the company expanded its Nicobar pigeon colony to 36 birds and produced essential germ cells, a key step toward creating dodo‑like birds. The launch attracted backing from XPRIZE founder Peter Diamandis, who announced a new VC firm, NeoGenesis Capital, to support Colossal’s programmable biology platform across health, agriculture, and conservation.
key_points: GenoMorph AI platform identifies gene edits for extinct species with limited genomes, focusing on the dodo
Colossal has found ~2,300 potential dodo cranial targets and will test them using lipid‑nanoparticle delivery
Nicobar pigeon colony expanded to 36 birds and essential germ cells produced
Peter Diamandis backs Colossal via NeoGenesis Capital
